messages:
maya: Heads up — I have a prod request_id=0b1f9a that the customer saw fail, but I can't find any raw request logs in the console for that id. trace link shows a span but no pod logs. Anyone seen this pattern?
kevin: Do you have the trace_id too or the target service? console sometimes samples fields.
maya: trace_id=8a7c4e3b, hit service edge-proxy-1 in us-west, time ~2024-11-12T22:10Z. Console trace UI shows spans from the edge -> router -> backend, but clicking the trace doesn't surface raw log lines.
kevin: First quick checks: 1) open tracing UI (Jaeger) and search the trace_id, expand the final span to see the pod name/host. 2) If you have the pod, run stern/ kubectl logs to tail the proxy around that time — console can drop fields due to truncation or sampling.
rafael: Also try searching the raw log index in Kibana/ES by request_id or trace.id — sometimes the console index alias differs. Example ES-style queries: 
```
request_id:"0b1f9a" OR trace.id:"8a7c4e3b"
```
If you want CLI fastpath: 
```
kubectl -n prod get pods -l app=edge-proxy -o name
stern edge-proxy -n prod -c proxy --since 1h | rg "0b1f9a"
```
sophie: small tip — some proxies use header names like x-request-ref or X-Request-Id. If the edge side generates a different header, grep for the path or user id instead. Example: 
```
kubectl logs -n prod $(kubectl get pods -n prod -l app=edge-proxy -o jsonpath='{.items[0].metadata.name}') -c proxy --since=60m | jq -R 'select(test("0b1f9a|8a7c4e3b"))'
```
infra-bot: runbook: https://intranet.redwood/runbooks/logs-traces-correlation (auto-sent) — steps for console vs kibana vs kubectl.
kevin: If nothing shows up on the proxy, check the ingress (LB) logs and CDN layer too — sometimes requests are dropped upstream and never reach pods. Also look for traceparent/x-cloud-trace-context on the trace spans.
maya: Ran stern and found a match — pod edge-proxy-1-5f8d, the log line shows the request id under header x-request-ref and the backend returned a 502. snippet: 
```
2024-11-12T22:10:03Z edge-proxy-1-5f8d proxy INFO "GET /api/v1/generate" status=502 req_id=0b1f9a user_id=1234
```
kevin: Nice. Next: correlate that timestamp with the backend pod logs (router/backends) using the pod name and time window. If you can't find backend logs, scope to the cluster egress or resource OOM/killing events.
sophie: If you're saving this for an on-call handoff, paste the stern line + pod name + the trace link. that'll speed up escalation.
maya: pasted snippet + trace link in the ticket. thanks all :thumbsup: — marking resolved for now.
